KANAL

240minutes
76solder joints
difficulty

A three-knob USB MIDI controller running OpenDeck

Heat the pad and the pin together for two seconds. Feed solder into the joint, not onto the iron. Take the solder away first, then the iron.

Strip 3 mm, twist the strands, and tin the end before you solder it to a pad.

Unplug USB and disconnect any battery before you solder or change a wire. Work on a surface that does not burn, and wash your hands after handling solder.

25KANAL-WIRE-1

Before you switch it on

  1. Look. Every joint is a shiny cone. No solder touches a neighbouring pad. No stray strands of wire.
  2. These must not beep. Set the multimeter to continuity and probe each pair. A beep means a short: find it before you plug in.
    3V3GNDADC_VREFGND
  3. These must beep. Probe the two ends of every connection.
    3V3Pico 3V3 · Display VCC · Encoder +
    GNDPico GND.8 · Display GND · Encoder GND
    I2C_SDAPico GP16 · Display SDA
    I2C_SCLPico GP17 · Display SCL
    ENC_APico GP2 · Encoder CLK
    ENC_BPico GP3 · Encoder DT
    ENC_PUSHPico GP6 · Encoder SW
    ADC_VREFPico ADC_VREF · Knob 1 3 · Knob 2 3 · Knob 3 3
    GNDPico AGND · Knob 1 1 · Knob 2 1 · Knob 3 1
    KNOB_1Pico GP26 · Knob 1 2
    KNOB_2Pico GP27 · Knob 2 2
    KNOB_3Pico GP28 · Knob 3 2
    BUTTON_1Pico GP7 · Button 1 1
    BUTTON_2Pico GP8 · Button 2 1
    BUTTON_3Pico GP9 · Button 3 1
    BUTTON_4Pico GP10 · Button 4 1
    GNDPico GND.3 · Button 1 2 · Button 2 2 · Button 3 2 · Button 4 2 · LED 4 K · LED 3 K · LED 2 K · LED 1 K
    LED_1Pico GP14 · R1 220 ohm 1
    r1_2R1 220 ohm 2 · LED 1 A
    LED_2Pico GP15 · R2 220 ohm 1
    r2_2R2 220 ohm 2 · LED 2 A
    LED_3Pico GP22 · R3 220 ohm 1
    r3_2R3 220 ohm 2 · LED 3 A
    LED_4Pico GP21 · R4 220 ohm 1
    r4_2R4 220 ohm 2 · LED 4 A
  4. Plug in. Nothing gets warm, nothing smells. If something does, unplug at once and go back to step 2.
  5. Flash the bring-up test. It reports every part it can find before you load the real firmware.pio run -e bringup -t upload && pio device monitor
26KANAL-WIRE-1

Kanal is built

Kanal is a small desk controller for a DAW or a soft synth: three knobs, a clickable encoder, four buttons with their own LEDs and a status display. It runs the open-source OpenDeck firmware on a Raspberry Pi Pico, so every control is mapped to MIDI in a browser, with no code. It is wired by hand from standard parts and lives in a printed case.
